deep_dive.title: GraphMemix: Query-Aware Evidence Forests for Long-Term Multimodal Agent Memory
deep_dive.abstract: Organizing long-term memory for multimodal agents remains challenging because existing methods either suffer from expensive question-agnostic offline summaries or naive embedding similarity matching that introduces incomplete and redundant context. To address these issues, we propose GraphMemix, a combinatorial-optimization graph memory framework that models memory organization as query-aware evidence-forest construction. Specifically, our method consists of three key components:(1) candidate graph construction, which expands multi-view seed memories through schema and semantic relations to acquire query-aware original context; (2) evidence utility and activation costs, which decouples direct memory support from anchor-conditioned relation verification to suppress redundant or conflicting information; and (3) forest optimization, which jointly selects a forest-format memory context under a maximum evidence budget and its reliable relational structure. By organizing memory into a query-relevant subgraph, the method avoids substantial lifecycle cost and recovers low-similarity complementary evidence. Experimental results across four long-term multimodal memory benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements with different foundation models and establish a new Pareto frontier between accuracy and lifecycle cost.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 针对多模态智能体长期记忆组织困难、离线摘要代价高且嵌入匹配引入不完整冗余上下文的问题，提出GraphMemix组合优化图记忆框架，将记忆组织建模为查询感知的证据森林构建；通过候选图构建、证据效用与激活代价解耦等关键组件，获取查询感知的原始上下文，在减少冗余的同时提高了长期记忆检索的针对性和完整性。实验证明该框架能够有效组织多模态长时记忆，为智能体上下文管理提供新思路。

deep_dive.title: Towards Reliable, Generalizable, and Specific In-Context Knowledge Editing via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
deep_dive.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful but limited by static parametric knowledge that becomes outdated once pretraining ends. Knowledge editing addresses this problem by updating model behavior on target facts without full retraining. In particular, in-context knowledge editing has gained attention because it is training-free and readily applicable to black-box LLMs. Recent reinforcement learning (RL)-based approaches improve over fixed retrieval strategies by adapting prompt construction to the quantity-quality trade-off. Despite initial success, they fail to model the prompt as a structured entity under the distinct and often competing objectives of reliability, generality, and specificity. Previous methods largely optimize a single objective and make decisions over only part of the prompt construction process, thereby overlooking both the balance of different objectives and the global organization of demonstrations. We propose Multi-Objective In-context Knowledge Editing (MO-IKE), a multi-objective RL algorithm that formulates prompt construction for in-context knowledge editing as a Constrained Markov Decision Process. MO-IKE trains a dynamic retriever to optimize competing objectives in knowledge editing, enabling more balanced and globally coherent prompt construction. On Llama-3.2, MO-IKE improves edit success (reliability) from 85.0% to 92.0%, paraphrase consistency (generality) from 77% to 79%, while increasing retention rate (specificity) by 23.0% compared to prior RL-based methods.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: In-context knowledge editing requires prompt construction balancing reliability, generality, and specificity. The paper models the prompt as a structured entity and uses multi-objective RL to optimize it, improving black-box LLM editing.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 大语言模型的参数化知识容易过时，上下文知识编辑希望在不重新训练的前提下更新目标事实，但现有方法难以权衡可靠性、通用性与特异性。本文将提示视为结构化实体，提出用多目标强化学习同时优化这些相互竞争的目标，并自适应地构建用于知识注入的上下文。实验表明该方法在多种编辑任务上提升可靠性、泛化性和特异性，并适用于黑盒模型。这项工作为面向智能体的上下文优化提供了一种可参考的多目标RL框架。
